definition: In natural language processing (NLP), a text graph is a graph representation of a text item (document, passage or sentence).
details: It is typically created as a preprocessing step to support NLP tasks such as text condensation term disambiguation (topic-based) text summarization, relation extraction and textual entailment.

explainer.lead: A text graph is a graph representation of a text item such as a document, passage, or sentence. It matters because it enables NLP tasks like topic-based term disambiguation, summarization, relation extraction, and textual entailment.

tiers.eli5: It turns a piece of writing into a network of connected dots, where the dots are parts of the text and the links show how they relate.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build text graphs as a preprocessing step so downstream tasks can operate over structured relations instead of raw strings. The pitfall is that graph construction choices constrain which downstream tasks work well.
tiers.paperLevel: A graph representation of a text item (document, passage, or sentence), typically created as a preprocessing step to support tasks such as text condensation term disambiguation, text summarization, relation extraction, and textual entailment.

explainer.example: A document is converted into a graph whose nodes and links are then used as input for summarization.
